name: Repository + Google Drive Artifact Synchronizer
sprintRole: Synchronize the active repository's use-case-relevant durable artifacts with the user's Google Drive workspace while preserving explicit source-of-truth direction, privacy boundaries, idempotent mappings, and conflict-safe proof
useWhen: The current project or use case spans a repository and Google Drive and the relevant plans, reports, handoff documents, spreadsheets, presentations, evidence packs, exports, or other durable artifacts need to be brought into a deliberate synchronized state without mirroring the whole repository or relying on one project-specific workflow.
inspectFirst: The active repository and current task/use-case context; repository governance and artifact/output registries, manifests, generators, operator docs, tracked reports and relevant handoffs; existing Google Drive project/workspace folders and mapped files when accessible; prior sync receipts or stable Drive identities; current Git/default-branch state; privacy/secret/ignored-file rules; and any explicit source-of-truth or publication contract for each candidate artifact.
expectedOutput: A bounded repository-to-Drive synchronization of only the artifacts relevant to the active use case, plus an evidence-backed sync ledger/receipt that records each artifact's repository identity, Drive identity or location when safe to record, authority/direction, action, resulting version/proof, conflicts or skips, and remaining user-only gates without duplicating workspaces or silently overwriting divergent truth.
nextStep: Resolve the active repository and use-case artifact set, discover or reuse the existing Drive workspace, classify authority and sync direction per artifact, execute every safe deterministic sync action, read back both sides, and repeat until every relevant artifact is current, unchanged, explicitly skipped, conflicted, or blocked by a named user-only gate.
proofGate: The active repo and Drive workspace are resolved from current evidence; every relevant candidate artifact is dispositioned; canonical repo artifact contracts determine scope rather than a whole-repo mirror; existing Drive identities are reused when available; private/secret/excluded material is not published; each write is read back; two-sided divergence is never silently overwritten; Google-native and repo-native source formats retain explicit authority; the sync receipt matches observed post-sync state; and no blanket completion claim exceeds the evidence actually verified.
copyContent:
SYNCHRONIZE THE ACTIVE REPOSITORY'S RELEVANT ARTIFACTS WITH GOOGLE DRIVE. DO NOT MIRROR THE WHOLE REPOSITORY, CREATE DUPLICATE PROJECT WORKSPACES, OR SILENTLY OVERWRITE DIVERGENT TRUTH.

Repository: resolve the active repo from current environment/link/path/context.
Use case: recover the current request and accessible relevant context; do not make the user restate it.
Google Drive workspace: use an explicit folder/file when supplied; otherwise discover and reuse the most strongly evidenced existing workspace before creating anything new.
Owned scope: use-case-relevant durable artifacts, their repo↔Drive mappings, safe sync actions, and sync receipt/proof.
Forbidden scope: whole-repo backup, Drive-as-source-control, secrets/private/ignored inputs, dependencies/caches/temp trees, unrelated Drive cleanup, silent destructive overwrite, unauthorized sharing changes, lossy round-trips without a contract, or unrelated domain logic.

MISSION
Own the generic repository↔Google Drive synchronization seam. Keep authority explicit, synchronize per artifact, and make durable project context available where it belongs. Google Drive is a collaboration/artifact workspace; Git remains repository history.

1. RESOLVE CURRENT TRUTH
Refresh repo/provider truth and resolve default branch, current head, overlapping work, canonical artifact registries/manifests/generators, and relevant outputs. Resolve Drive from connected evidence; search existing workspace/files before creating uploads. Reuse stable Drive identities. If Drive access, account, or permission is unavailable, name the exact external gate and do not claim a sync.

2. BUILD THE RELEVANT ARTIFACT SET
Do not sync every tracked file. Use the current use case plus canonical repo evidence to select only durable plans/specs, decisions, reports, client-safe docs, spreadsheets, presentations, evidence packs, exports, manifests, handoffs, or intentional Drive-facing references that materially support the work. Exclude implementation source unless explicitly published, plus secrets, credentials, private/protected data, ignored local state, vendor/dependency trees, caches, build debris, and temporary logs.

3. CLASSIFY AUTHORITY BEFORE COPYING
Assign each candidate exactly one authority:
- REPO-AUTHORITATIVE — repo source may publish/update Drive; Drive edits do not silently flow back.
- DRIVE-AUTHORITATIVE — Drive owns content; repo consumes only an approved export/reference.
- BIDIRECTIONAL-BY-CONTRACT — both may change only under an explicit lossless conversion/merge/conflict contract.
- DERIVED / PUBLISH-ONLY — generated/presentation artifact flows from its producer to Drive and is not a competing editable source.
- PRIVATE / DO-NOT-SYNC — intentionally excluded.
Unknown authority is UNKNOWN/CONFLICT. Do not pick a winner by recency alone.

4. MAP IDENTITIES, NOT JUST FILENAMES
For each relevant artifact map repo canonical path/registered identity, Drive file/folder identity or stable location when safe, authority, format, last proven versions/hashes/timestamps when available, and intended action. Prefer stable Drive identity to name-only matching. Treat ambiguous same-name files as a resolution problem, not permission to create another copy. Keep sensitive Drive IDs out of tracked repo state when policy requires private receipt storage.

5. PRESERVE FORMAT AUTHORITY
Do not call lossy Google Docs/Sheets/Slides export-import round-trips synchronized. Preserve Google-native authority when Drive owns the document. Preserve repository-native authority when Markdown, source workbook, presentation source, structured data, or generated artifact owns the content. Export/import only under an explicit conversion contract. A PDF/render is normally publication output, not editable canonical source.

6. PLAN THE SYNC LEDGER
For every relevant artifact choose one action: UPLOAD, UPDATE DRIVE, DOWNLOAD/IMPORT, UPDATE REPO, NO CHANGE, CONFLICT, or SKIP. Record:
artifact | repo identity | Drive identity/location | authority | pre-sync evidence | action | post-sync evidence | status/gate
Every material candidate appears once. `Drive synced` without per-artifact accounting is not proof.

7. EXECUTE SAFE, IDEMPOTENT ACTIONS
Reuse the existing project folder and mapped file. Update in place when identity and authority are clear; do not create `copy`, `(1)`, dated duplicate, or a new project folder merely because resolving identity is harder. Preserve canonical repo paths/contracts. Do not use Drive as source control. Drive→repo changes use approved import/conversion plus normal branch/validation/integration rules. Repo→Drive publishes the exact validated source/artifact required by its contract. Do not delete, rename, move, transfer ownership, or broaden sharing without current explicit authority.

8. FAIL CLOSED ON TWO-SIDED DIVERGENCE
Before overwrite, determine whether both mapped sides materially changed since the last common/proven state when evidence permits. If both changed and no deterministic merge/precedence contract resolves them, mark CONFLICT, preserve both truths, identify competing versions, and name the smallest user decision or owning merge mechanism. Timestamp-newer alone is not a safe conflict resolver. Missing comparison evidence lowers proof; it does not authorize overwrite.

9. READ BACK AND VERIFY
After each Drive write, re-list/read the target and verify existing identity, intended content/version/metadata, and workspace location. After repo writes, verify the canonical file/artifact at exact head, run focused owner validation/build, and integrate authorized green work. Verify generated artifacts against their current generator/input floor. A successful write call alone is not completion proof.

10. SECOND PASS TO A BOUNDED FIXED POINT
Re-scan relevant repo artifacts and Drive from the opposite direction for moved/renamed files, stale exports, duplicates, one-sided updates, conflicts, or items that should be PRIVATE/SKIP. Execute newly safe deterministic actions and read back again. Stop when every in-scope item is current/no-change, synchronized, skipped, conflicted, or blocked by an exact external gate.

BOUNDARIES WITH SPECIALIZED WORKFLOWS
This generic owner does not absorb project-specific management, billing, roster, taxonomy, evidence-language, or reporting semantics merely because a project uses Drive. Preserve any stronger specialized synchronizer's domain authority; apply this prompt only to generic mapping/sync mechanics.

FINAL REPORT
Report repo/default branch and repo proof level; Drive workspace; artifact/status counts; reused vs created files/folders; authority-class counts; uploads/updates/imports/no-change/conflicts/skips; validation/readback proof; repo commit/PR/merge state; unresolved conflict/privacy/access gates; proof ceiling; and first executable next action. Do not expose secrets or unnecessary private Drive identifiers.
